blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At executive level, double taxation treaties are strategic instruments, not merely technical tools. They shape which countries a company can realistically do business in, how much the business earns after tax, and how quickly relief can actually be claimed when something goes wrong. The senior leader's task is not to memorise treaties but to know which ones the company relies on, which ones might change, and what happens if they do.

Treaties evolve. Political relationships shift. A treaty that was generous ten years ago may be renegotiated into something far less favourable. A company whose strategy depended on a particular treaty — and that had not planned for its possible change — can find itself quietly exposed when the renegotiation lands.

Had we modelled the alternative treaty scenarios last year, the expansion plan would have looked different. The best senior tax leaders treat treaties the way a navigator treats weather forecasts — studied carefully, respected fully, and planned around, not assumed.

items.q: According to the text, at executive level double taxation treaties are best understood as…
options: the responsibility of external advisers alone
strategic instruments, not merely technical tools
fixed arrangements that rarely change
documents to be memorised in full
items.why: "double taxation treaties are strategic instruments, not merely technical tools."

items.q: What does the text say is the senior leader's actual task regarding treaties?
options: To memorise the wording of every treaty
To delegate all treaty questions to the tax team
To renegotiate treaties personally with governments
To know which treaties the company relies on, which might change, and what happens if they do
items.why: "to know which ones the company relies on, which ones might change, and what happens if they do."

items.q: Why can a company find itself "quietly exposed"?
options: Because it never signed any treaty at all
Because it relied on a treaty and had not planned for its possible change
Because its navigators ignored the weather
Because it paid tax in too many jurisdictions
items.why: "A company whose strategy depended on a particular treaty — and that had not planned for its possible change — can find itself quietly exposed."

items.q: The sentence "Had we modelled the alternative treaty scenarios last year, the expansion plan would have looked different" suggests that…
options: the expansion plan has already been cancelled
the scenarios were not modelled, and the plan may now be flawed
the scenarios were in fact modelled and the plan was sound
modelling scenarios makes no difference to planning
items.why: Inferência: o condicional passado (Had we…) marca algo que NÃO foi feito — daí o plano ter sido construído sobre uma base frágil.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Treaty risk should be modelled before an expansion decision.
A generous treaty can later be renegotiated into a less favourable one.
Political shifts can change the value of a treaty.
Once a treaty is signed, its benefits can be safely assumed for years.
items.why: Inferência: a tese central é que tratados evoluem e não devem ser 'assumidos' — o navegador planeja em torno deles, não os toma como garantidos.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James conduzindo a revisão de cenários dos tratados. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, let's not treat this as a compliance exercise. We rely on three treaties more than any others, and the whole point of today is to ask a single question about each one: what happens to us if it is renegotiated in the next two years?

Take the first. The withholding relief we claim on intercompany flows sits entirely on that treaty. Had the previous board stress-tested it before we built the São Paulo structure, we would have hedged the exposure. They didn't, so the exposure is live, and it is larger than the finance pack suggests.

The second treaty is politically fragile. I'm not predicting it changes — I'm saying that if the relationship cools, the relief could be capped, and our after-tax margin in that corridor would move sharply. I want a modelled number on that, not a reassurance.

So here is what I need from each of you by Friday. One page per treaty: what we depend on, what a plausible renegotiation looks like, and what it would cost us. If we can't answer that, we are navigating on yesterday's forecast.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What single question does James want asked about each treaty?
options: Which lawyer originally drafted it
How much it saved the company last year
What happens if it is renegotiated in the next two years
Whether it was signed correctly
items.why: "what happens to us if it is renegotiated in the next two years?"

items.q: What does James say about the withholding relief on the first treaty?
options: The exposure is live and larger than the finance pack suggests
It was renegotiated last month
It no longer applies to intercompany flows
It is fully hedged and carries no risk
items.why: "the exposure is live, and it is larger than the finance pack suggests."

items.q: What does "Had the previous board stress-tested it… we would have hedged the exposure" imply?
options: The previous board did not stress-test it, so the exposure was left unhedged
Stress-testing the treaty was impossible at the time
The previous board did stress-test it and hedged successfully
The exposure has already been resolved
items.why: Inferência: o condicional passado (Had they… we would have…) indica que o teste NÃO foi feito e, por isso, a exposição ficou aberta.

items.q: Regarding the second treaty, what is James's actual point?
options: He believes the treaty is politically safe
He is certain the treaty will change soon
He wants to renegotiate it himself
He wants a modelled cost of a plausible change, not a reassurance
items.why: Inferência: "I'm not predicting it changes… I want a modelled number on that, not a reassurance." Ele pede quantificação do risco, não previsão.

items.q: What does James mean by "we are navigating on yesterday's forecast"?
options: The finance team is working too slowly
The company is planning against outdated assumptions
The weather is affecting the São Paulo office
The treaties expire tomorrow
items.why: Inferência: a metáfora do navegador — decidir sobre tratados sem cenários atualizados é como navegar com uma previsão vencida.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "At board level a treaty is a strategic instrument, shaping where we can profitably operate." A strategic instrument is…
options: a legal penalty imposed by a regulator
a piece of office equipment
a routine accounting entry
a tool used deliberately to advance high-level objectives
items.why: Strategic instrument = instrumento estratégico: algo usado de forma deliberada para atingir objetivos de alto nível.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "When double taxation occurs, the treaty lets us claim ___ so the same income is not taxed twice."
options: exposure
relief
forecast
renegotiation
items.why: Relief = alívio (fiscal): o mecanismo que evita a bitributação da mesma renda.

items.q: "Our entire structure relies on that single treaty." To rely on something means to…
options: publish it externally
quietly ignore it
depend on it for support or success
renegotiate it every year
items.why: To rely on = depender de: contar com algo como base de apoio.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "If the ___ between the two governments cools, the treaty could be capped."
options: political relationship
accounting standard
reporting line
weather forecast
items.why: Political relationship = relação política: é o que, ao esfriar, pode disparar a renegociação.

items.q: "A company that had not planned for change can find itself exposed." Here, to be exposed means to be…
options: fully compliant with every rule
exempt from all taxation
vulnerable to a risk it has not protected against
publicly praised for its planning
items.why: To be exposed = ficar exposto: vulnerável a um risco contra o qual não se protegeu.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de estratégia fiscal. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the revised treaty strategy." To sign off on means to…
options: formally approve it
quietly shelve it
comment on it informally
leak it to the press
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Two directors pushed back on the exposure estimate." They…
options: forgot to read it
approved it without question
rewrote the whole treaty
resisted or challenged it
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "We agreed to model the scenarios but never followed through." This means we…
options: changed the treaty text
finished ahead of schedule
delegated it to the auditors
failed to carry the task to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Let's stress-test each treaty against a plausible renegotiation." To stress-test means to…
options: translate it into another language
examine how it holds up under adverse conditions
sign it as quickly as possible
reduce the number of clauses
items.why: Stress-test = submeter a cenários adversos para ver como aguenta a pressão.

items.q: "A reassuring memo alone won't move the needle on our real exposure." This means it will…
options: cost far more than expected
trigger an immediate renegotiation
take years to draft
make no meaningful difference
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, produzir diferença perceptível.
